cr_data.provenance:
Georgia O'Keeffe, Abiquiú, New Mexico. 
1959, Dr. Helen Boignon, New York. 
1979, The Museum of Modern Art, New York, purchased from a private collection 
(Helen Boignon?), New York through Hirschl & Adler Galleries (Norman Hirschl), New York. (Source: MoMA, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, March 1946. . . . No signature." Abiquiú Notebooks indicates, "Back: O'Keeffe writing 'White Line – Blue Abstraction' – 27. 40 x 30 Initials and star" [not verified]. Abiquiú Notebooks after 1977 indicates, "Sold to the Museum of Modern Art by Hirschl & Adler Galleries, 1979." (Source: Lynes, 1999)

credit_line: The Museum of Modern Art, New York. Acquired through the Helen Acheson Bequest
description: A central, rounded form dominates the composition. The shape is surrounded by thin, rippling forms in dark blue, pale blue, white, and yellow that resemble petals wrapped around the center of a flower. Running through the center of the composition from top to bottom is a thin strip of white similar to a crack in a mirror. On either side of the strip, the forms are slightly different in color and shape as though refracted.
imageCaption: Courtesy of Museum of Modern Art (MoMA).
